requirements.text: Once everything is done, close the case

Case Ready State Verification.evidence: an exact duplicate of Case Closure Verification's query (status = closed_complete on the same case), carried jointly by the closure requirement, which names both; its description's pass through ready cannot be read from the final state. disagreement: A excluded, B excluded, both as the duplicate; chose kept because an exact-duplicate check whose cells are all carried is kept jointly, not excluded

notes: Merged from two passes that agree on every requirement, cell and value (case 61 for Travis Wood 11 with COE Talent Management, account TRANSFER-TW-2025, priority moderate, a valid source; task 150 of type checklist; both closed_complete; notifications to travis.wood@servicenow.com and his manager randy.martinez94@servicenow.com, selected by case and recipient; hr_profile 11 position Administration) and on seven of eight dispositions. disagreement: Case Ready State Verification: A excluded, B excluded (an exact duplicate of Case Closure Verification); kept, carried jointly by the closure requirement, because the current rule keeps an exact-duplicate check whose cells are all carried. The acting user Karen Watkins (user 39) has role admin; policy section 2 says an Administrator must not perform routine HR case work, but every benchmark check expects the case to be created and closed, so the file assumes the work is done. The policy's enumerations disagree with the seed (priority moderate vs medium; channel chat_bot/walk_in vs chat/walk-in; roles admin/agent vs administrator/hr_specialist); where they differ the seed's spellings are used. No stay requirements: the request forbids nothing and no selector has a boundary (Travis Wood is the only Travis and the only Wood in the seed). Least sure (both passes): the notification addresses, kept at the benchmark's user.email although every seed notification uses personal_email.
